name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +18 partisan lean
Incumbent Latimer running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win near certainty
model.rationale: The district's +18 Democratic lean, Latimer's incumbency and fundraising advantage, and a little-known, unfunded Republican challenger all point to a lopsided Democratic win; markets agree at roughly 96% for Democrats.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Latimer would be the first sign this race is closer than its fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-16 is a heavily Democratic Westchester-area seat where first-term incumbent George Latimer is seeking reelection. The district's partisan lean of about 18 points Democratic gives Republicans a steep structural hurdle, and Latimer has the advantages of incumbency and a solid fundraising total, with over $660,000 raised and cash on hand heading into the fall.

Republican Joseph Cinquemani reports no fundraising and has drawn little outside attention, and no independent groups have spent in the race. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-20s.
